control_comparison.note: cep-10 shares the toolchain=unavailable/path=restricted profile but exited 1 with output, so its signature IS present. The flag tracks whether output existed to match, not whether the fault was injected.

df-15_reclassification.consequence: A_u denominators are not comparable across the S23.2 / exp-3 boundary (8 unknown cases -> 7).

flagged_cases.action: NO QUARANTINE; record as a difficulty characteristic
flagged_cases.rationale: Exit 127 means the toolchain binary was never found, so the verifier produced no output for a textual signature to match against. The fault did manifest (exit != 0) and is directly observable via inspect_environment (toolchain=unavailable, path=restricted). This is materially different from the df-04 defect class the owner review repaired, where the exit code was 0 and no fault had been injected at all.

residual_risks.detail: all three flagged cases are `environment` and present the model with a bare exit-127 and no verifier output. They are plausibly harder from the base context alone, so `environment` results should be stratified by signature presence in any future replication.

df-06's inspect_target_binding reports all_exist=false because default test discovery cannot resolve when the toolchain is missing, so df-06 is gate-eligible for verification_plan as well as environment. Legitimate (the gate is a sufficiency test, not an oracle) but it must not be read as a second injected fault.
for exit-127 faults the flag cannot fire by construction. Corpus gates must not treat it as evidence of a construction defect.
